summary: Private deployment: confirm and change log retention setting
body:
Description

Customer asks to (a) confirm current retention for Private deployment operational logs and (b) increase retention to meet policy requirements.

Context
- Customer is running Redwood Private (VPC) with in-cluster log storage.
- They were told on a security review that Private retention is customer-controlled, but they want the default values and recommended approach documented.

Current behavior / defaults (per installer values)
- Operational logs in the in-cluster log store: 30 days retention by default.
- Redwood control-plane access logs (support access): 90 days retention in Redwood systems.
- Redwood audit logs: 365 days retention in Redwood systems.

Customer request
- Increase Private operational log retention from 30 days to 180 days.
- Confirm whether any request/response payloads are retained (answer: no persistent storage by default; debug payload logging is optional and if enabled, default retention is 7 days).

Comments

Connor OBrien (Support)  2025-02-19
Opened on behalf of NorthPeak. They need explicit numbers for their internal policy doc.

Naomi Feldman (Security)  2025-02-20
Please ensure we distinguish: (1) customer-side retention in Private (configurable) vs (2) Redwood-side control-plane logs. Use 30d/90d/365d/7d/14d language as in Confluence.

Hiro Tanaka (Eng, Private Deployments)  2025-02-24
Confirmed Helm values: log retention is set via `logStore.retentionDays` and defaults to 30. Customer can set to 180; storage sizing needs review.

Resolution
- Provided customer guidance to set `logStore.retentionDays=180` and scale storage accordingly.
- Confirmed Redwood control-plane access logs: 90 days; audit logs: 365 days.
- Confirmed debug payload logging (if enabled): 7 days by default; Hosted/Dedicated operational request logs (metadata): 14 days (not applicable to Private unless customer forwards logs to Redwood, which they are not doing).
